theme: Feature flags: turning features on, off and out slowly

terms.definition: A setting that turns a feature on or off without shipping a new version of the app.
terms.example: Hide the new tab behind a feature flag.

terms.definition: A remote setting that lets you turn a broken feature off right away for every user.
terms.example: Flip the kill switch, checkout is crashing.
terms.code:
var checkoutOn = true
checkoutOn = false // kill switch
print(checkoutOn)

terms.definition: A release plan that shows a new feature to a small share of users first, then to more over time.
terms.example: Start the gradual rollout at ten percent.
terms.code:
let userID = 42
let percent = 10
print(userID % 100 < percent)

video.title: Feature Flag, Kill Switch & Gradual Rollout | Day 235
video.description:
Learn to explain how teams hide, release and stop a feature without a new app version: Feature Flag, Kill Switch & Gradual Rollout, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Feature Flag - A setting that turns a feature on or off without shipping a new version of the app.
Kill Switch - A remote setting that lets you turn a broken feature off right away for every user.
Gradual Rollout - A release plan that shows a new feature to a small share of users first, then to more over time.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Feature Flag, Kill Switch & Gradual Rollout in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Feature Flag, Kill Switch, Gradual Rollout 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Feature Flag - A setting that turns a feature on or off without shipping a new version of the app.
한국어: Feature Flag: 앱의 새 버전을 내지 않고도 기능을 켜거나 끄는 설정

Kill Switch - A remote setting that lets you turn a broken feature off right away for every user.
한국어: Kill Switch: 문제가 생긴 기능을 모든 사용자에게서 즉시 꺼 주는 원격 설정

Gradual Rollout - A release plan that shows a new feature to a small share of users first, then to more over time.
한국어: Gradual Rollout: 새 기능을 먼저 소수의 사용자에게 보여 주고 점차 늘려 가는 출시 방식

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about how to ship a new screen safely with a flag, a gradual rollout and a quick stop, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Feature Flag, Kill Switch and Gradual Rollout in English?

dialogue.title: Ship it, but safely

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the new home screen is ready, but design wants it next week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hide it behind a feature flag. A feature flag turns a feature on or off without a new app version.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The code ships now, and we flip the feature flag later.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if the new pay screen has a bug?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we need a kill switch. A kill switch turns the broken feature off right away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does the kill switch need an App Store update?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, that is the point. The app reads the value, and everyone is safe in minutes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can we show the new home to everyone at once?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better not. Use a gradual rollout, and start with a small share of users.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then ten percent, then more if the numbers look good?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. A gradual rollout plus a kill switch is a safe way to ship.
